sampling_model.design: Complete randomization assigns exactly \(n_a\) of the \(N\) fixed units to each arm \(a\in\mathbb A\); the design is known and assignment is the only randomness.
sampling_model.units: The potential-outcome schedule \(x\in[0,1]^{3\times N}\) is fixed. The deterministic rounding theorem conditions on the full armwise empirical marginals \(F\); the statistical layer observes only one potential outcome per assigned unit.
sampling_model.treatment: The observed outcome is \(x_{Z_i i}\), and the estimator is the fixed contrast of arm means \(\widehat\theta_N=\sum_ac_an_a^{-1}\sum_{i:Z_i=a}x_{ai}\).
sampling_model.overlap: Every arm size is positive and \(n_1+n_2+n_3=N\); endpoint consistency assumes \(n_a/N\to p_a\in(0,1)\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each \(F_a\) is estimated by the simple-random-sample empirical law \(\widehat F_a\), then lifted to the equal-weight \(N\)-point law \(G_a\). Sampling error is controlled in \(W_1\) by exact hypergeometric variance, separately from deterministic rounding loss.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The paper obtains the exact partial identified set by optimizing over all marginal-compatible couplings and proves plug-in convergence for quadratic costs.
Lemma 1 gives sharp two-arm covariance bounds attained by comonotone and countermonotone quantile couplings.
The paper exhibits failure of the discrete quadratic Monge ansatz and asks for rigorous quantification of its error.
Theorem 3 proves strong NP-completeness of complete mixability, while the approximation result controls a bottleneck row sum.
The paper computes variance-maximizing causal completions by integer programming for broad assignment mechanisms and estimator classes.
Theorem 2.2 classifies the extreme points of the symmetric three-marginal, three-state Kantorovich polytope and includes non-Monge vertices.
Algorithm 3 rounds an approximately feasible tensor to the fractional transportation polytope, not to a Monge schedule.

body.tldr: Fractional multi-marginal transport can produce a sharper-looking three-arm variance bound than any \(N\)-unit potential-outcome table can realize. For the bounded scalar contrast \(c=(1/4,1/4,-1/2)\), the worst same-empirical-marginal discrepancy is exactly of order \(N^{-1}\): an optimal-support dual-slope geometry, nested basic-table freezing, and hierarchical marginal repair give a deterministic bit-polynomial schedule with loss at most \(3456/N\), while an explicit four-row obstruction padded by isolated dummy rows loses exactly \(1/(46080N)\) for every \(N\ge4\). Under complete randomization this becomes a computable \(O(N^{-2})\) band around the sharp upper variance endpoint. Armwise empirical quantile lifts consistently estimate both variance endpoints while retaining the larger sampling-without-replacement error as a separate term.

project_justification.gap: Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025) formulate causal variance bounds over fractional multi-marginal couplings, whereas a finite population requires one common \(N\)-row schedule. Emami and Pass (2025) demonstrate discrete non-Monge optimality and request quantitative error bounds, but in a different quadratic orientation. Haus (2015) treats exact mixability and bottleneck approximation, and Brennan et al. (2025) rely on integer programming without an analytic realization width.
project_justification.niche: The unfilled object is the worst additive loss between a fractional optimum and an \(N\)-row optimum for the same three bounded empirical marginals and a fixed causal squared-contrast cost, together with a construction whose complexity is polynomial in rational input length.
project_justification.fill: The project derives an ordered dual-slope interval lemma, a multiscale exact-marginal repair algorithm, an all-\(N\) rational lower family, and design-based endpoint certificates with explicit sampling-without-replacement plug-in error.

body.related_work: Emami and Pass (2025, Introduction, Example 1, and Discussion) move from the empirical Kantorovich relaxation to Monge implementability, prove a minimal non-Monge quadratic example, and explicitly identify quantitative approximation error as future work; their barycenter cost has the opposite squared-sum orientation from the signed scalar contrast here. Friesecke (2019, Theorem 2.2 and Section 3) analyzes non-Monge extreme points in a symmetric finite transport polytope but does not give an all-denominator additive rate. Gao, Ge, and Qian (2025, Sections 2--3 and Theorem 1) identify causal bounds with fractional multi-marginal transport and prove plug-in rates; Theorem \(\mathrm{thm:variance-certificate}\) shows why their fractional endpoint can fail to be an \(N\)-row finite population and supplies an explicit band. Haus (2015, Theorem 3 and the approximation section) proves hardness of exact matrix mixability and a bottleneck PTAS, objectives that do not subsume additive average squared-contrast rounding. Altschuler and Boix-Adser\`a (2023, Algorithm 3) restore exact marginals after approximate tensor optimization but remain inside the fractional transportation polytope. Puccetti and Wang (2015, Theorem 1.1 and Section 5) provide the rearrangement representation and document unresolved higher-dimensional negative-dependence geometry; their discretization comparison changes the marginals rather than imposing same-\(N\) row realizability. Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014, Lemma 1 and equations (7)--(11)) give sharp two-arm variance endpoints, recovered exactly by \(\mathrm{prop:two-arm-reduction}\). Brennan et al. (2025, Sections 2--3) compute finite completions for general designs by integer programming and motivate an analytic certificate in the present restricted geometry. Li and Ding (2017, Theorems 3--4) supply the fixed-potential-outcome complete-randomization framework, while Hammer et al. (1996) provide a concrete multi-arm trial consumer.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The universal constant \(3456\) is deliberately loose and can be numerically uninformative at ordinary trial sizes; the useful report is the actual primal--dual width \([C_{\mathrm{alg}}(F)-V_{\mathrm{rel}}(F)]/(N-1)\). The exact large-\(N\) constant and extremal geometry remain open. The plug-in uncertainty band uses a first-moment Markov argument rather than a nonsmooth transport limit law, so sampling error dominates deterministic rounding error under proportional allocation.
body.honest_scope: The sharp order, explicit constants, all-\(N\ge4\) lower family, rational bit-polynomial algorithm, variance translation, and plug-in endpoint bounds are all to be proved. The theorem does not assert that one experiment observes all three full marginals, that every interior variance in the interval hull is attained, or that the unknown actual completion has variance at least \(U_{\mathrm{lo}}(F)\). The exact value of \(\Delta_3\) is outside the asymptotic theorem. The standard two-arm case has zero realization loss by Birkhoff integrality and reduces to Aronow, Green, and Lee (2014).
